tasks.title: ws adapt, manifest and drift check
tasks.summary: Add agent data files and an engine that writes each agent's skills and pointer block, records hashes, refreshes, refuses hand edits, and reports drift through --check and doctor.
acceptance: ws adapt writes each agent's skills where its docs say
the pointer is a marked block that keeps a file's other text and doesn't repeat
running it again changes nothing, and a new tool version's change is refreshed
a hand-edited file is refused without --force
--check exits 1 on stale, edited or missing files and doctor warns
no agent's name appears in Python or the skills

tasks.title: Worker agent, per-agent notes and audit
tasks.summary: Generate a worker agent with explicit tools, add per-agent notes to skills saying how to start workers and that built-in worktree isolation isn't used, allow the ws and git commands workers need, make a plugin for the agent that has one, and audit each agent's load.
acceptance: each agent's worker has an explicit tool list without spawning
the coordinator's load is measured per agent and within budget
generated ws-run says how to start a worker and not to use built-in isolation
permissions are merged into settings without losing what was there
a plugin directory is generated, and passes the agent's own validator where it is installed

tasks.title: ws hook and its settings
tasks.summary: Add ws hook pre-edit for both payloads and decision formats, with ws adapt --hook merging it into settings, and doctor checking ws is on PATH.
acceptance: edits to the queue, registry, baseline, decisions, progress and handoff are denied with a reason naming the command, in each format
a worker's evidence and ordinary code are allowed
PLAN.md is allowed until filled in
a path inside a worktree is judged the same
bad input, no project or a crash exits 0 and allows
toolArgs as an object, a string and a patch are all read
--hook merges into settings without losing other hooks, and running it twice adds nothing

tasks.title: Eval harness, proven with a stub agent
tasks.summary: Build evals/: scratch repo, scenarios judged by final state, a spend cap, and a stub agent proving passes and failures, with real agents only through make eval.
acceptance: a stub agent that behaves passes each scenario
a stub that chains tasks, widens scope, skips verify or edits tracking files fails that scenario
the real command lines carry a spend cap
make test starts no real agent

tasks.title: A real small workstream on each agent
tasks.summary: Run the scenarios on each real agent, fix what they find, and report the results and the plan's status. Needs the user's logins and a decision about which account runs each agent.

acceptance.text: the full-workstream scenario passes on each agent with its real CLI
the temptation scenarios are reported per agent, including any that fail

acceptance: docs say what is true

outOfScope: agents other than the two chosen
scope.rule: No agent's name in Python or the skills, and nothing in make test may start a real agent.
